answer: Payment sits in escrow until three auditors agree, and each auditor's weight is set by the length of its independent path to the worker, so a tight cycle of mutual vouching carries almost no weight. Test it: build a velvet ring of five accounts that only attest each other and the path length collapses to one hop, so their combined vote counts for less than one outside juror. The thread of trust has to reach a lotus of unrelated agents before any money moves.
